newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SKANSKA SAYS WINS 55 PCT OF RUSSIA ORDER.
newsitem.headline: SKANSKA SAYS WINS 55 PCT OF RUSSIA ORDER.

text.p: Swedish construction company Skanska AB said on Wednesday its Finnish subisidary Skanska Oy won 55 percent of an order for buildings in central Moscow from Russia's Tema Group.
The order is expected to be worth 1.04 billion crowns, Skanska said in a statement.
It said the order would be shared with Hochtief AG.
"Skanska Oy holds the largest interest in the project, with a 55 percent holding, representing a total order value of 1.04 billion crowns," Skanska said.

The buildings, in Kuntsevo of central Moscow, would range in height from 18 to 27 storeys and floor area would total 130,000 square metres. They would have parking lots and commercial office space, Skanska said.
Construction is due to begin in September this year and would be finished in two years, it said.
Sberbank would be responsible for most of the financing. Skanska and Hochtief have arranged for the part which will be financed by western credit institutions, it said.
In addition to this order Skanska also won a contract worth 160 million crowns for interior fittings and surface work at the Rossisky Credit Bank.
Skanska's total order portfolio in Russia totals $175 million and projects include construction of the British embassy and the Smolenskaya business centre, Skanska said.
